why: rclcpp blocks the calling thread until the first `/clock` message arrives. RFC-0021 forbids a blocking helper that does not drive the executor -- a wait that spins nothing stops the transport for as long as the simulator takes to publish, and on a single-threaded executor that is forever. The predicate it waits on IS available (`Clock::started`, issue 0789): a node polls it from a timer, or simply publishes once time is non-zero.
